headline: Chip Surge Powers a Split Market as Geopolitical Fires Burn Beneath the Surface
body_html:
Thursday's mid-session tape is sharply divided, with semiconductors and semiconductor equipment names doing the heavy lifting while healthcare, consumer, and software stocks drag in the opposite direction. Of 519 names tracked, 297 sit in the red against 220 in the green, confirming that the advance is narrow rather than broad. The Semiconductors sector leads all groups with a gain of roughly 5.3%, while Software and Consumer are the day's worst performers, off 1.7% apiece.

The standout mover of the session is FormFactor, surging more than 24% to pace the gainer board, with Lam Research close behind at nearly 20% and Sandisk adding 17%. The equipment and memory theme is unmistakable, apparently catching a tailwind from Samsung's second-quarter operating-profit beat on AI chip demand disclosed overnight. On the downside, Alnylam is the session's sharpest loser, shedding more than 24%, while Omnicell and Sonos each fall roughly 14%.

Macro cross-currents are adding complexity into the afternoon. A continuing Treasury sell-off — following the Federal Reserve's divided decision to hold rates steady — is keeping rate-sensitive sectors under pressure, and drone strikes near the Suez Canal and at a Mediterranean port are injecting fresh geopolitical uncertainty. Watch whether the chip rally can sustain breadth into the close or whether the macro headwinds reassert themselves.

briefs.headline: Samsung Earnings Spark Semiconductor Equipment Rally
briefs.body: Samsung Electronics posted second-quarter operating profit that topped analyst estimates, citing soaring demand for AI chips. The result appears to be the catalyst behind Thursday's broad surge in semiconductor and equipment names, with FormFactor, Lam Research, and Sandisk among the sharpest beneficiaries mid-session.

briefs.headline: Drone Strikes Near Suez and Mediterranean Port Elevate Shipping Risk
briefs.body: A drone struck two vessels at a Mediterranean port, Egyptian authorities confirmed, as a separate attack near the Suez Canal raised fresh alarm about energy-infrastructure security. The incidents represent an apparent widening of hostilities and add a new layer of uncertainty for global shipping routes that markets are still pricing in.

briefs.headline: QatarEnergy Moves to Plug Hormuz Gap With US LNG Purchases
briefs.body: QatarEnergy has quietly secured 33 US liquefied-natural-gas cargoes to compensate for shipments disrupted by Hormuz tensions, according to sources. Separately, a QatarEnergy-controlled tanker became the first vessel to exit the strait in nearly three weeks, a development traders are watching closely for signs of easing supply pressure.

briefs.headline: Shell Posts Near-Record Quarterly Profit as Conflict Lifts Crude Prices
briefs.body: Shell reported second-quarter profit that more than doubled to $9.8 billion, the second-highest result on record, as the Iran conflict pushed energy prices higher. Oil itself is trading in choppy fashion Thursday, edging lower amid Oman-Iran diplomatic talks even as the broader geopolitical backdrop remains tense.

briefs.headline: Treasury Sell-Off Persists After Fed Holds Rates on a Split Vote
briefs.body: US Treasuries extended their losing streak following the Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged, with the vote internally divided. The continued rise in yields is weighing on rate-sensitive sectors including healthcare and software, which rank among Thursday's worst-performing groups in early afternoon trade.

briefs.headline: Gold Firms as Dollar Slips and Fed Uncertainty Lingers
briefs.body: Gold edged higher in mid-session trading, drawing support from a softer US dollar — which weakened against the yen as focus shifted toward upcoming inflation data — and persistent uncertainty over the Fed's next move. Wealth managers are navigating the crosscurrents alongside a growing challenge: clients increasingly turning to AI chatbots for financial guidance.
